original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: Generic common-B mutable-source connector for every n>=1 with all 2^n-1 outputs: prove minimum Q=n+1 and the exact minimum R at that Q; construct and completely price the n=5 unequal-tariff witness.
scope_change_reason: The paid source-XOR extension is established by PR1340/1370. Follow PR1524 unequal Q/R price handoff using a new query-count/readout-count slice, rather than repeat equal-price or fixed ten-query results.
bottleneck_link: Changing the boundary operation alphabet can trade expensive common-map queries for inexpensive readouts; this is an abstract recursive-interface result requiring a real hosted boundary before supplier use.
stop_rule: One approximately 60-minute session; prove or falsify the affine-prefix rank argument, construct the smallest five-source witness, verify dirty/free-factor maps and complete invoices, then stop without claiming global unequal-price optimality.
evidence: README all-n proof; deterministic CERTIFICATE/RESULT; complete formal dirty root/expanded/inverse maps, n=1..9, 168 GL3 bases, 168 full-span circuits, 12 semantic controls; second dense oracle 7360 executions and 2 concrete controls; 7 CLI/source/receipt/relocation/regeneration test groups.
author: Arham Tahir
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof, code, tests and writing; no subagents or independent human review.

open_questions.question: What is the minimum source-XOR count at six Q and 96 R?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would sharpen this endpoint's price when source mutation is expensive.
open_questions.first_step: Project onto closed GL(5,2) source words and identify a six-vector full-span query circuit in their exposed row directions.
open_questions.blocked_by: Eight X is attained; no exhaustive source-restoration census or all-word XOR lower bound is supplied.

open_questions.question: Where can this unequal-price common-B boundary be legally hosted?
open_questions.why_it_matters: An abstract favorable tariff does not establish supplier savings.
open_questions.first_step: Trace one real boundary with expensive shared B and cheap A_m, exclusive temporary source ownership, and price ports, routing, frames, precision, storage and dispatch.
open_questions.blocked_by: No physical supplier instance or complete physical tariff is established.
